scope: Controlled Qt6/Kvantum state comparison for scrollbar endpoint arrows versus a wholly insensitive scrollbar, under the active KDE semantic palette.

contract.whole_widget_insensitive: separate state using KDE insensitive roles

environment.platform: offscreen; real Qt Widgets and installed Kvantum plugin

method.measurement: 15x15 arrow-cell pixel color histograms plus scrollbar values before/after clicks
limitations: Offscreen rendering verifies the installed style and input state, but is not an on-screen visual acceptance test.
The script uses allocated scrollbar geometry for horizontal cell crops because the offscreen subControlRect query returned the origin for both horizontal line controls.
Hover and pressed glyph relief were not measured in this state test.

implementation_analysis.runtime_result: At a range endpoint, Kvantum paints the unavailable arrow with the same disabled-role appearance used when the entire scrollbar is disabled. Input remains blocked correctly.
implementation_analysis.configuration_limit: Kvantum theme configuration exposes scroll_arrows as a presence toggle, not an independent range-boundary versus whole-widget-insensitive artwork state.

source_explanation.note: This upstream checkout is explanatory and is not claimed to be the exact Debian 1.1.4-3 source. The installed plugin's output was tested directly.

implementation_analysis.conclusion: The authorized SVG-and-metrics-only I171 scope cannot give a range-boundary arrow the parent's normal palette while preserving the separate insensitive appearance: both are mapped to the same disabled SVG state by the installed style. This needs a style-level state distinction or a revised design rule; neither was changed here.

next: Wait for a separately authorized scope if changing Kvantum style code or revising the endpoint color contract; meanwhile continue only another already authorized independent queue item.
